% RETURN, REBASED · EOD 2026-08-06
CYCLICALS LEADCyclicals +3.6% vs defensives on the month
Rotation ReadCitrini · claude

The rotation is a cyclical energy bid swallowing the AI momentum trade whole, and you need to be in the laggards turning leaders right now. XLE leads every sector with a 10.65% one-month return and 28.78% year-to-date, while XLK bleeds 3.01% in one month despite holding 23.38% YTD. The theme baskets confirm the same pattern from the other side: Energy stocks average 10.1% over one month with PSX leading, SaaS averages 11.9% with PYPL on top, and Software averages 9.9% with HUBS driving. Semis and AI infra, the YTD champions at 61.4% and 79.2%, are getting hammered at 9.5% and 7.0% one-month respectively. NVDA still leads Semis but the basket is uniformly distributed lower, and ARM sits in the bottom of AI infra while ANET holds the top. The laggards today are last year's winners, and the winners are the stuff you would buy if you expected a soft landing with sticky inflation.

The central tension is whether this is healthy broadening into neglected cyclicals or the first crack in a regime where risk assets survive only by rotating. Defense at 0.9% one-month and 0.3% YTD, Banks at 0.1% and 11.3%, and Industrials at 0.6% and 23.6% all tell you late-cycle money is searching for a home without committing to anything speculative. Fintech at 0.1% one-month and 14.2% YTD negative, with HOOD as the laggard, shows zero appetite for speculative financial leverage. Quantum at 13.2% one-month and 28.6% YTD negative is a full breakdown. Uranium at 6.7% one-month and 22.5% YTD negative with OKLO in the bottom tells you the long-duration thematic bid is gone. GLP-1 at 5.8% one-month with VKTX lagging confirms even healthcare thematics are losing institutional sponsorship.

The stretched ratios tell you this rotation is not a short-term squiggle. It is a regime shift at the cross-asset level. HYG/LQD sits at a z-score of 2.72 in the top 1% of its yearly range, SHY/TLT at 2.68 in the top 1%, and SPY/TLT at 2.41 in the top 1%. These are not marginal readings. They say high yield is outperforming investment grade at an extreme, short-duration is crushing long-duration at an extreme, and equities are destroying long bonds at an extreme simultaneously. TLT/SPY at 2.22 in the bottom 1% of its range confirms the haven trade is broken from the other side. XLI/XLU at 2.14 in the top 1% with a 12.85% YTD move puts the cyclical-over-defensive trade at a stretched extreme that either confirms the expansion or marks the exact point where you trim cyclicals into strength.

Cyclical rotation is running at cross-asset extremes while the AI momentum trade rolls over, and the question is whether broadening survives without the megacap crutch.

BULL

Energy at 10.65% one-month, Industrials at 15.94% YTD, and XLI/XLU at z-score 2.14 confirm a pro-cyclical expansion backed by credit strength. HYG/LQD at 2.72 says high yield investors see no default risk.

BEAR

Semis at 9.5% one-month, AI infra at 7.0%, and XLK at 3.01% negative say the growth engine is stalling. Quantum at 13.2% and Uranium at 6.7% one-month show long-duration speculative appetite already unwinding.

TELL

XLI/XLU at z-score 2.14 in the top 1% of its yearly range. If it breaks below that level, the cyclical bid is fading and you rotate defensive. If it holds, the expansion leg has further to run.

⚠ XLI/XLU at z-score **2.14** in the top **1%** says cyclical outperformance over defensives is at an extreme, confirmed by Industrials YTD at **15.94%** versus Utilities at **2.73%**. vs XLI itself is down **1.29%** over the past month while XLU is down **2.08%**, meaning the ratio is holding on old momentum, not fresh cyclical buying.: Trust the one-month deterioration. The ratio is stretched on fumes. If Industrials do not reclaim positive one-month momentum soon, XLI/XLU reverts and the cyclical leadership signal fails.
⚠ SaaS at **11.9%** one-month and Software at **9.9%** one-month show risk appetite rotating into growth-adjacent tech, a broadening signal. vs XLK is down **3.01%** one-month and Semis are down **9.5%** one-month, showing the core tech complex is unwinding at the same time.: Trust the theme baskets over the sector ETF. PYPL leading SaaS at **11.9%** and HUBS leading Software at **9.9%** are laggard-catch-up trades, not momentum extensions. The broadening into neglected software is real but it is low-beta money, not a new growth leg.

The Credit and Rates block is the loudest signal on the page, and it is confirmed trend, not a reversion candidate. HYG/LQD at z-score 2.72 in the top 1% of its yearly range, SHY/TLT at 2.68 in the top 1%, AGG/TLT at 2.58 in the top 1%, and JNK/TLT at 2.55 in the top 1% all say the same thing from four angles: investors want yield and credit exposure, and they are dumping duration at an extreme pace.

TLT/IEF at 2.56 in the bottom 1% confirms long bonds are underperforming intermediates at a stretched level, which is a trend you accept until the Fed changes tone. SPY/TLT at 2.41 in the top 1% with a 17.44% YTD move and SPY/IEF at 2.14 in the top 1% extend the same risk-on, duration-off message across equities versus bonds.

The one ratio that looks like a genuine mean-reversion candidate is XLI/XLU at 2.14 in the top 1% with a 12.85% YTD move. Industrials have only fallen 1.29% this month while Utilities fell 2.08%, so the ratio is stretched mostly on prior momentum, not fresh buying.

If Industrials continue to weaken while Utilities stabilize, this pair reverts fast and signals the cyclical rotation is exhausting. XLC/SPY at 1.96 in the bottom 7% of its range with a 14.12% YTD decline is confirmed trend, not a reversion setup.

Communication Services has been a laggard all year and nothing in the one-month 1.03% return suggests a bottom.
